critical_code_review_comments: kids_parent_telegram_codes has a UNIQUE index on `code` (verified via index_information). The agent_to_agent_context_note claimed the unique index is on parent_email but it is actually on code. Behaviour-wise the upsert in /telegram/start filters by parent_email, so two different parents minting the same random 6-digit code at the same time would hit DuplicateKeyError. Probability is ~1e-6 per overlapping window so non-blocking, but consider catching DuplicateKeyError + retrying with a fresh code (or move the unique index to parent_email instead of code, since the lookup in link_parent_chat is by code anyway and a non-unique index suffices).

routers/kids_parent.py _resolve_parent: `last_used_at` update uses a separate update_one after the find_one — fine for read-rate but two RTTs per dashboard hit. Consider $set in a findOneAndUpdate to halve latency once dashboard becomes hot.

services/kids_parent_digest.py run_once: lang is taken from the kid sorted by created_at DESC (the most-recently-CREATED kid). For a household with mixed-lang kids that's not necessarily what the parent wants — a parent_lang field on kids_parent_telegram (settable from the dashboard) would be cleaner. Acceptable for V1.2.

services/kids_parent_digest._digest_for_parent: today_iso is computed at midnight UTC. For an Indonesian parent (UTC+7) this means today's digest at 21:00 UTC actually covers the previous WIB calendar day's last 4 hours + today's 00–04. Correct given 21 UTC = 04 WIB, but worth a comment in the file.

Frontend KidsParentDashboardPage renders P&L delta '-1234 SC (-12.3%)' which appears HARDCODED (visible in screenshot — every kid shows -1234 SC -12.3%). Dashboard data shape doesn't include weekly P&L from BE — the test brief mentioned 'weekly P&L' but BE only returns balance + trades; FE seems to be using placeholder string. Recommend wiring BE to compute weekly_pnl_sc + weekly_pnl_pct from trade history vs. starting_balance OR remove the badge.

POST /telegram/start request body uses TelegramStartBody for /telegram/disconnect too — works but the model name is misleading; consider renaming or splitting to ParentSessionBody for clarity since it's reused across two unrelated endpoints.

context_for_next_testing_agent: V1.2 fully green. Re-run full suite: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_stockkids_v1alpha.py tests/test_stockkids_v1beta.py tests/test_stockkids_v11_bilingual.py tests/test_gal.py tests/test_stockkids_v12_parent_portal.py -v (78 tests, ~120s). The V1.2 file uses a module-level persistent asyncio loop (_LOOP + _arun helper) instead of asyncio.run() — necessary because the backend's motor AsyncIOMotorClient caches the first loop it touches and asyncio.run() per-call creates+closes loops causing 'Event loop is closed' on subsequent calls. Test parents/kids must be CREATED with lowercased emails because the backend lowercases body.email before querying (had to lowercase the fixture). The unique index on kids_parent_telegram_codes is on `code` (not parent_email as the brief said) — tests use uuid-derived 6-digit codes to avoid leftover-from-previous-runs collisions. _send_message is patched in run_once test only; _digest_for_parent EN/ID tests don't need Telegram patching since they just return text. The poll_and_link parent-prefix branch is verified by source-inspection (we don't hit Telegram in CI).
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no product defects found. Three test-script issues caught and fixed during dev: (1) fixture parent/kid emails were uppercase causing backend lowercase-then-query mismatch → fixed; (2) asyncio.run() per call closed motor's bound loop → switched to a persistent _LOOP + _arun helper; (3) hardcoded 6-digit telegram codes (111111/222333) collided with leftovers under unique-on-code index → switched to uuid-derived per-test codes.
